brief:
The Quincy Institute contends that the Israel lobby exerts outsized influence over American foreign policy decisions and domestic civil liberties protections, according to analysis from the think tank. The institute examines how lobbying efforts tied to Israeli interests affect U.S. strategic priorities in the Middle East and the scope of political speech and dissent at home.

The analysis reflects ongoing debate over the role of pro-Israel advocacy groups in shaping U.S. policy toward the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the Middle East region more broadly. Critics of such lobbying say it constrains foreign policy options; supporters argue advocacy groups represent legitimate constituents with shared interests.
title: Israel lobby shapes U.S. foreign policy and civil liberties, Quincy Institute argues
